name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link** at the top of every page, visible by default.

This ensures keyboard users bypass repetitive navigation blocks in one jump, solving a critical barrier for screen reader and motor-impaired users. The trade-off is a small permanent UI element that takes up space, but its value in accessibility far outweighs minimal layout impact.

name: Reader
text: A large, always-visible skip link steals focus from the main content for sighted users and risks being invisible to screen-reader users who rely on focus order. Instead, make the skip link appear only when tabbed to—it remains hidden until needed, preserving screen real estate and respecting focus flow. Test with a screen reader and keyboard-only users to confirm it’s discoverable and doesn’t disrupt navigation.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a **large, high-contrast skip link that only appears when keyboard focus reaches it**—it stays hidden until needed.

This solves the core problem: sighted keyboard users get the bypass they need without cluttering the page, while screen reader users still detect it through focus order. The trade-off is a brief visual flash when tabbed to, but that’s a small price for universal usability.

name: Reader
text: A skip link that only appears on focus risks being invisible to screen-reader users who rely on visual cues—many screen readers announce elements only when they’re rendered visible. Instead, pair it with an ARIA `aria-hidden="false"` toggle or a zero-opacity state that screen readers still announce, then fade it in on focus. Test with VoiceOver/NVDA and a keyboard-only user to confirm it’s both discoverable and unobtrusive.

name: Access
text: DECISION: Implement a **persistent, zero-opacity skip link** that becomes visible on keyboard focus (via `opacity: 0` → `opacity: 1` transition) and is announced by screen readers via `aria-hidden="false"`—owned by accessibility-w1.
